title: Suggestions (Optimize) Beta — Risk & Quality Guardrails
author: Selene Huang
body:
## Purpose
This document defines the *quality and safety guardrails* for the Redwood Console **Suggestions** view (beta) for batching/caching cost optimizations. It answers:
- Which recommendation candidates must be **suppressed** (not shown to customers) and why.
- How we compute and monitor **regression signals** (quality, latency, reliability) tied to a suggestion.
- What **evaluation coverage** is required before a suggestion type can be surfaced.
- **Alerting + auto-disable** criteria for the beta cohort.

This is written for Applied ML/Evals, Console + suggestions-service engineering, telemetry/analytics, and SRE.

## Scope
**In scope (beta):**
- Suggestions that recommend *configuration changes* for **batching** and **caching**.
- Read-only UI (no one-click apply). Suggestions may still influence behavior via manual customer changes, so we treat surfacing as a safety-sensitive action.

**Out of scope (beta):**
- Model swaps, quantization changes, routing policy changes.
- Automated apply workflows (phase 2). Phase 2 requires additional pre-apply validation gates and reversible rollout controls; some requirements below anticipate that work.

## Definitions
**Suggestion:** A recommendation object shown in Console scoped to (tenant, workspace, route, model, region). It includes a savings estimate and risk fields.

**Risk level (Low/Medium/High):** Derived per ADR-0274; UI displays a single label + rationale bullets.

**Suppressed suggestion:** A suggestion candidate generated by the backend that is intentionally not returned to the Console list API due to guardrail violations.

**Telemetry freshness window:** Maximum age of baseline metrics allowed for surfacing estimated savings.

## Guardrail design principles
1. **Do no harm by default:** If signals are missing, stale, conflicting, or ambiguous, prefer suppression over guessing.
2. **Explainability:** If we cannot provide a customer-readable rationale (what/why/assumptions), we do not surface.
3. **Conservative bias in beta:** We optimize for trust and correctness over coverage.
4. **Tenant isolation:** No cross-tenant signals, aggregates, or “similar customer” inference in suggestion generation.

---

## 1) Suppression rules (do not surface)
Suppression is evaluated in the suggestions-service *before* returning results to Console. Each suppressed candidate must have a `suppression_reason_code` recorded internally for audit/debug.

### 1.1 Hard suppression (always suppress)
| Code | Category | Condition | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| SUPPRESS_NO_TELEMETRY | Data | No baseline token/cost + request metrics for the scoped route/model/region | Cannot estimate savings or risk without baselines |
| SUPPRESS_STALE_BASELINE | Data | Baseline metrics older than **24h** (default; configurable) | Week-over-week estimate drift and “phantom savings” reported by beta users when baselines were stale |
| SUPPRESS_LOW_VOLUME | Data | Fewer than **50k tokens/day** or < **200 requests/day** over trailing 72h | Estimates unstable; risk calibration unreliable |
| SUPPRESS_TENANT_CONFIG_LOCKED | Safety | Tenant has admin policy `optimize_suggestions_disabled=true` or environment disallows suggestions | Respect customer and deployment policy |
| SUPPRESS_PRIVACY_SCOPE | Security | Suggestion would require displaying disallowed fields (e.g., prompt content, user identifiers) | Console must only show aggregated, privacy-safe basis |
| SUPPRESS_UNSUPPORTED_RUNTIME | Platform | Route uses runtime mode not covered by batching/caching controllers (e.g., legacy engine) | Avoid recommending changes that are no-ops or misapplied |
| SUPPRESS_CONFLICTING_REC | Methodology | Recommendation conflicts with a higher-priority or mutually exclusive recommendation already active for same scope | Avoid double-counting and contradictory actions (see ADR-0275) |

### 1.2 Conditional suppression (suppress unless additional criteria met)
| Code | Category | Condition | Unsuppress criteria |
|---|---|---|---|
| SUPPRESS_HIGH_WORKLOAD_VARIANCE | Risk | Coefficient of variation for concurrency or input length > threshold (see ADR-0274) | Require explicit rationale bullet and risk>=Medium; also require eval slice for long-context and burst workloads |
| SUPPRESS_LATENCY_HEADROOM_LOW | Risk | p95 latency headroom < **10%** to tenant’s configured SLO (or default SLO if none) | Only surface if recommendation is fully reversible and predicted p95 impact <= 3% and risk=High |
| SUPPRESS_QUALITY_SIGNAL_UNKNOWN | Quality | No offline eval coverage for the model family + feature (cache/batch) combination | Must pass required eval suite (Section 3) |

### 1.3 Recommendation-type specific suppression
#### A) Batching suggestions
Suppress when any of the following are true:
- Route has **streaming** enabled and the proposed batching mode is known to increase time-to-first-token beyond beta thresholds without a compensating benefit.
- Observed request time distribution indicates **ultra-low latency** usage (median < 150ms end-to-end), and batching would materially increase queueing.
- The model is in a class where batching controller is not validated (new architecture without eval coverage).

#### B) Caching suggestions
Suppress when any of the following are true:
- Prefix stability is low: estimated cache hit-rate confidence < threshold (per risk model).
- Workload contains high entropy prefixes (e.g., unique user/session prefixes) such that caching likely degrades memory pressure without wins.
- Cache key space would be dominated by long contexts causing eviction churn; if we cannot quantify eviction pressure, suppress.

---

## 2) Regression signals: computation & monitoring
We track regressions at two levels:
1) **Population-level:** Is the beta harming overall tenant experience?
2) **Suggestion-scope level:** For a specific (route/model/region) where a recommendation was surfaced and later adopted, did anything regress?

### 2.1 Events and attribution (required)
Telemetry must emit privacy-safe events:
- `suggestion_impression` (shown in list)
- `suggestion_opened` (detail drawer viewed)
- `suggestion_adopted` (customer-confirmed change detected; may be inferred by config diff or explicit future “apply” action)
- `suggestion_dismissed` (optional in beta)

Attribution rules:
- We attribute regressions to adoption only after detecting an adoption timestamp `t0` and comparing **pre-window** vs **post-window** metrics.
- Default windows:
  - Pre: [t0-24h, t0-1h]
  - Post: [t0+1h, t0+24h]
- If traffic volume is insufficient in the pre/post windows, the regression result is marked **inconclusive**.

### 2.2 Quality regression signal (offline + online proxies)
Because most batching/caching changes should not change model outputs directly, we still require quality monitoring for:
- Hidden truncation/timeout behavior changes
- Increased error handling/fallback frequency
- Latency-induced truncation (clients timing out) altering effective outputs

**Quality regression composite (QRC):**
- Offline eval delta (when applicable):
  - Use standardized prompt set evaluation (see Section 3).
  - Compute `Δquality = quality_score_post - quality_score_pre` (model- and task-specific).
- Online proxy deltas (always applicable):
  - `Δtimeout_rate`
  - `Δfallback_rate` (requests served by fallback model/region)
  - `Δtruncation_rate` (server-side max_tokens reached unexpectedly or client aborts correlated with latency increases)

**Beta fail thresholds (any triggers alert):**
- `timeout_rate_post >= timeout_rate_pre + 0.25%` (absolute)
- `fallback_rate_post >= fallback_rate_pre + 0.50%` (absolute)
- Offline eval: `Δquality <= -0.5%` for “stable” tasks, or `Δquality <= -1.0%` for “noisy” tasks (task tags defined in eval plan)

### 2.3 Latency regression signal
**Primary:** p95 end-to-end latency for the scoped route/model/region.
- `Δp95 = (p95_post - p95_pre) / p95_pre`

**Beta fail thresholds:**
- Alert if `Δp95 >= +8%` and absolute p95 increase >= 50ms.
- Alert if time-to-first-token (TTFT) increases >= 100ms for streaming routes.

**Notes:**
- We do not auto-disable solely on latency drift if traffic patterns changed (burst vs steady). The alert must include a variance check and SRE review.

### 2.4 Reliability regression signal
**Primary:**
- 5xx rate
- 429 rate (rate limiting triggered unexpectedly)
- OOM/eviction churn (for caching) signals from runtime

**Beta fail thresholds:**
- `5xx_post >= 5xx_pre + 0.10%` (absolute) OR p95 suggestions-service latency breaches (see Section 4)
- Runtime OOM events increase >= 2x on the affected pool within 6h of adoption

### 2.5 “Trust” regression (estimate stability)
Even if performance is fine, we treat wildly unstable estimates as a beta issue.
**Estimate stability checks:**
- Savings estimate changes > **30% week-over-week** for same scope without an explained telemetry reason (traffic mix shift) should generate a product/ML alert.
- Confidence score must degrade (not improve) when telemetry is missing; if confidence remains high despite missing baselines, treat as a bug.

---

## 3) Required evaluation coverage before surfacing
A suggestion type can only be shown in Console if it has:
1) **Offline eval coverage** for representative models/workloads.
2) **Shadow-mode online validation** in at least one internal tenant or Redwood staging tenant.
3) **Guardrail checks** integrated into the suggestions-service gating logic.

### 3.1 Offline eval requirements
We require evals for each combination:
- Suggestion type: caching vs batching
- Deployment mode: Hosted + Dedicated (Private is allowed but must be validated separately due to config differences)
- Model family buckets: (A) Llama-class, (B) Mistral-class, (C) other newly onboarded architectures

**Minimum eval suite (per bucket):**
- Prompt sets:
  - Short-form chat
  - Long-context (>= 8k)
  - Tool/function calling style
  - RAG-like structured prompts (templated)
- Workload slices:
  - Steady concurrency
  - Burst concurrency
  - High variance input length

**Acceptance thresholds:**
- Quality: no statistically significant degradation beyond thresholds in Section 2.2.
- Latency: p95 increase <= **5%** under steady workloads for Low/Medium risk; High risk may exceed but must be labeled and suppressed unless explicitly allowed.
- Reliability: no increase in runtime error class rates beyond noise; OOM events must not increase.

### 3.2 Shadow-mode online validation
Before enabling a suggestion type for external beta tenants:
- Run for **7 consecutive days** in shadow mode:
  - Generate suggestions
  - Compute savings + risk
  - Do NOT surface in UI for external tenants
- Validate:
  - No cross-tenant leakage in query results
  - Baseline freshness pipeline meets SLO
  - Estimate stability meets thresholds

### 3.3 Documentation requirement (customer-facing explainability)
A suggestion must include:
- “What to change” (plain language)
- “Why it helps” (mechanism)
- “Where it applies” (route/model/region)
- “Basis of estimate” fields (aggregated metrics only)
- Risk rationale bullets and explicit assumptions

If any of the above is missing, suppress with `SUPPRESS_INSUFFICIENT_EXPLANATION`.

---

## 4) Alerting, auto-disable, and beta stop criteria
### 4.1 Service-level SLOs (suggestions-service)
We alert on the backend service independently from “user harm” metrics.

**SLO targets (beta):**
- Availability: **99.9%** (rolling 7d)
- Latency: p95 **< 400ms** for list endpoint; p95 **< 600ms** for detail endpoint
- Staleness: < **2%** of served suggestions with baseline older than 24h

### 4.2 Auto-disable triggers (feature flag kill switch)
The beta must support rapid shutdown via `suggestions_beta` flag and per-tenant allowlist.

**Auto-disable triggers (any):**
1) **Security/tenancy:** confirmed cross-workspace/tenant visibility bug (Severity 0).
   - Action: auto-disable globally immediately.
2) **Widespread reliability issue:** suggestions-service 5xx > **1%** for > 10 minutes in prod.
   - Action: auto-disable globally; page on-call.
3) **Staleness:** stale-baseline served rate > **5%** for > 30 minutes.
   - Action: auto-disable globally; open incident if sustained.

**Manual pause criteria (requires SRE + Product):**
- Multiple tenants report confusion or material mismatch: realized savings < 0 for >= 3 adopted suggestions in a week where confidence was “high”.
- Quality proxy regressions appear correlated with adoption across multiple tenants.

### 4.3 Incident classification for beta
- **Sev 0:** Data leak / tenant isolation breach → immediate shutdown and security incident process.
- **Sev 1:** UI/Service outage preventing customers from viewing Suggestions (not core inference) but causing widespread errors in Console.
- **Sev 2:** Significant correctness issue in savings/risk shown to customers (e.g., systematic 2x overestimation), no security impact.

---

## 5) Auditability and debugging requirements
For every suggestion candidate (including suppressed), record:
- suggestion_id, tenant/workspace identifiers (internal IDs)
- scope: route/model/region
- versioned schema IDs for savings + risk payloads
- baseline metric timestamps and freshness
- suppression reason code (if suppressed)
- risk inputs (high-level feature values; avoid raw customer identifiers)

**Access control:** Viewing detailed basis fields is governed by Console RBAC; access must be audit-logged (see ENG-2408).

---

## 6) Beta operational checklist (Applied ML/Evals sign-off)
Before enabling a new tenant cohort or a new suggestion subtype:
1) Offline eval suite passed and published in the eval report.
2) Shadow-mode validation completed (7d).
3) Suppression rules implemented with reason codes.
4) Alerts configured and tested in staging.
5) Runbook link attached in on-call dashboard.
6) Support FAQ updated to explain:
   - Why suggestions may be missing (insufficient telemetry / staleness)
   - Why risk may be High (with concrete factors)
   - Why estimates may change week-to-week (traffic mix)

- Applied ML/Evals: Selene Huang (quality guardrails), Jonas Weber (risk/savings methodology)

## Appendix A — Suggested suppression reason codes
- SUPPRESS_NO_TELEMETRY
- SUPPRESS_STALE_BASELINE
- SUPPRESS_LOW_VOLUME
- SUPPRESS_UNSUPPORTED_RUNTIME
- SUPPRESS_TENANT_CONFIG_LOCKED
- SUPPRESS_PRIVACY_SCOPE
- SUPPRESS_CONFLICTING_REC
- SUPPRESS_HIGH_WORKLOAD_VARIANCE
- SUPPRESS_LATENCY_HEADROOM_LOW
- SUPPRESS_QUALITY_SIGNAL_UNKNOWN
- SUPPRESS_INSUFFICIENT_EXPLANATION

## Appendix B — Default thresholds (beta)
- Baseline freshness: <= 24h
- Minimum volume: >= 50k tokens/day AND >= 200 req/day (72h trailing)
- Latency regression alert: +8% p95 AND >= 50ms absolute
- TTFT regression alert: +100ms (streaming)
- Timeout rate alert: +0.25% absolute
- Fallback rate alert: +0.50% absolute
- Suggestions-service global 5xx auto-disable: >1% for 10 min
- Stale-baseline served auto-disable: >5% for 30 min

(Thresholds are expected to be tuned during beta based on cohort feedback and observed variance.)
